method: Trace current source state transitions and evidence; inspect existing test code and existing recorded fixtures; run one isolated synthetic ledger/journal counterexample. Compare official Anthropic documentation. No provider API call, credentials or environment reads, product source changes or whole-suite test runs.
verdict: The non-test general-live guard remains justified. The current general SQL ledger already implements bounded same-scope reservation, request attempt fencing, unknown holds and late evidence; it is incorrect to say all shared-ledger mechanisms are absent. The legacy synthetic-approved live path instead uses a separate trials journal, and request-specific Anthropic billing reconciliation and a verified account-scope policy are not demonstrated. A persistent ledger-write failure may leave an unknown turn with a reserved rather than uncertain reservation, requiring an additional scope-level boundary test before live activation.

general_state_machine.scope: chat_general.py:151–153 maps actual live to project:<project ID>; test transport is a separate rehearsal-live project scope. Connection ID/revision are server declarations, not verified account identity (chat_general.py:91–114).
general_state_machine.admission: chat_general.py:389–433 checks exact manifest, current binding, rights, budget and reserves in the calling transaction. ledger.py:259–280 uses budget revision, holds+spent and maxConcurrentJobs to bound same-ledger reservations.
general_state_machine.submission: chat_general.py:515–537 uses BEGIN IMMEDIATE and require_bounded_exposure plus claim_attempt for each count/message; ledger.py:112–137 binds reservation, job, request and manifest hashes with a unique fenced attempt. ledger.py:211–224 blocks over-ceiling and uncertain reservations within the same workspace/scope. Ordinary reserved/sending work may run concurrently; same-scope admission is budget bounded, not globally serialized.
general_state_machine.observation: chat_general.py:540–612 records observed usage and attempt state, then uses estimate for live-style transport and settle for contract-fake. An estimate is not confirmed provider billing. Unknown and unsupported usage are not automatically priced; no inference from documentation examples about real omission frequency.
general_state_machine.loss_and_restart: chat_general.py:437–454 and 665–689 recover or mark attempts and reservations unknown/uncertain without automatic resend when the relevant writes succeed. ledger.py:154–199 records bounded, owner/hash-fenced immutable late observations and does not itself settle. An in-flight request can already have begun before another turns unknown; the guard cannot recall it.
general_state_machine.existing_test_scope: tests/test_ledger.py tests atomic competing reservations; tests/test_budget_crossflow.py and tests/test_budget_dispatch_guard.py use shared rehearsal-scope injection for synthetic generation/general-chat crossflow. tests/test_provider_attempts.py covers same-ledger claims, loss and late evidence in fixtures; test_chat_live_contract.py covers loopback behavior. Test source was read, not independently rerun here. These tests do not by themselves prove current legacy journal and general production ledger share a budget or account.

separate_legacy_journal.observation: Legacy ChatRuntime uses a caller-supplied journal_path SQLite trials table, with its own cumulative 50 USD cap and unknown live hold checks. General chat uses Store ledger budgets, reservations and provider_attempts. Even if files happen to share a filesystem, those independent tables/transactions do not maintain one common invariant. Same-conversation busy-turn checks do not create cross-journal cost accounting.
separate_legacy_journal.independent_fixture: In a TemporaryDirectory, mark a legacy UsageJournal live-mode trial as outcome_unknown with a 6 USD hold; separately create an ordinary Store ledger fixture budget of 10 USD, run require_bounded_exposure and reserve 6 USD. Output: legacy_unknown_hold_micro=6000000; general_admitted=True; general_held_usd=6; combined_nominal_usd=12; illustrative_shared_limit=10. This is a storage-level synthetic demonstration of absent cross-check, not a real provider transaction or evidence that the deployed configuration defines an identical shared 10 USD account cap. No real key, account, or external request.
separate_legacy_journal.interpretation: Until a common provider/account budget invariant is explicitly required and implemented, do not assert that both paths atomically share it. Legacy access is synthetic-only and separately approved, while actual general live is disabled.

write_failure_gap.fact: Existing test code expects persistent ledger-command failure to leave turn outcome_unknown and journal_failure=update_failed while the reservation stays reserved, including immediately after recover(). The exposure gate explicitly queries uncertain reservations and held+spent overflow, not general_chat_turns journal_failure/outcome_unknown associated with reserved reservations.
write_failure_gap.interpretation: Code review suggests a different conversation or flow in the same scope may pass that gate if capacity remains, after the write failure ends, despite unresolved exposure. A new actual concurrent/boundary reproduction was not executed in this review; same-conversation busy checks are separate. Before enabling live, test and close this scope-level failure path without discarding or silently settling its hold.

late_evidence_and_reconciliation.implemented: ledger.py:57–105 and contracts.py:24–67 provide project-scoped list/detail and authorized idempotent late-evidence review, with digest/revision checks. Allowed review outcomes are reviewed_pending_billing or conflicting_evidence; review does not settle or release the reservation.
late_evidence_and_reconciliation.missing_or_unverified: provider_billing.py:14–63 normalizes fal-billed generation_jobs, not Anthropic chat; no verified Anthropic request-specific settlement path was found in inspected source. Explicit response estimates and stored late usage are not invoices or verified per-request charges.
late_evidence_and_reconciliation.official: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/usage-cost-api describes organization-level Usage/Cost Admin APIs requiring an admin credential; cost data is grouped by day/workspace/description and can be delayed. Do not automatically allocate an aggregate bucket to an individual request or describe it as a request-specific invoice. https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/token-counting calls count an estimate; https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing describes tier, geography, caching and tool-dependent rates.
late_evidence_and_reconciliation.requirement: An explicit authenticated, attributable billing-evidence and safe manual/automated reconciliation policy is needed; where exact attribution is unavailable retain uncertainty or use an approved verified conservative bound rather than inventing a settlement. Provider/admin authorization is distinct from implementing and testing local state transitions.

scope_and_identity: connection_id and connection_revision are injected declarations (chat_general.py:91–114), and project budgets are independent. Neither proves account identity nor deduplicates aliases that access the same provider account. This is an unresolved policy/operating-boundary issue unless an account-wide hard cap has been promised; it becomes a safety defect if an account-wide limit is claimed without enforcing a shared budget. Decide whether the guarantee is only per project or also per provider account, then bind and test it. Do not infer provider identity from labels.

choices.option: A: one SQL budget and attempt state machine for both actual-live paths
choices.scope: Migrate or bridge legacy live admissions, claims and reconciliation to a shared authoritative budget/transaction boundary; preserve immutable existing evidence and idempotency. Choose account/project hierarchy explicitly.
choices.cost_and_risk: More migration and concurrency work; existing journal unknowns must be conservatively represented rather than discarded.
choices.acceptance: Synthetic race: both directions, different conversations, last-budget competition, already reserved work plus unknown, persistent journal write failure and restart, late response, exact-approval, no double-send and accounting conservation. Existing provider attempt and late-evidence APIs remain functional. Real account verification is a separate step.

choices.option: B: retain legacy exclusively as an isolated offline/synthetic test path and use common SQL ledger for general live
choices.scope: Enforce that the legacy runtime cannot send a real provider request and cannot share a real provider connection; prove this at actual adapter boundary. Keep general-live guard until same-scope write-failure recovery, reconciliation and chosen account/project budget policy are validated.
choices.cost_and_risk: Narrower change and clearer separation but eliminates legacy live trials; merely labeling its journal fake or changing a UI flag is insufficient.
choices.acceptance: Attempt to inject real Anthropic transport into legacy path and prove no external dispatch; demonstrate synthetic/live separation and all general ledger unknown/timeout/restart/late evidence cases with isolated transport.

recommendation: For the smallest local vertical slice consider B only if synthetic-only legacy scope is acceptable; otherwise choose A. Either path keeps the current non-test guard while local fixture work proceeds, and neither changes monetary caps or silently removes unknown holds. Separately, a user-authorized operator must establish provider account/workspace identity, model access, price and billing evidence; then conduct a bounded real workflow under explicit consent and independently verify received usage/reconciliation. Those external approvals are not supplied by this research.
unverified: No paid requests, actual model use, live account identity, actual invoice, comprehensive suite run, or end-user workflow performed. Existing fixture tests show test intention; they are not production receipts.
